findings.text: L3 monitoring domain combines a generic header with a cache instance number. It tracks busy monitoring identifiers through a bitmap pointer and holds per bandwidth event state pointers. Two deferred works handle overflow and limbo with separate designated processors, and a counter configuration pointer holds assignment state.

Cache capability describes mask width through cbm_len and minimum set bits through min_cbm_bits with shareable portion through shareable_bits. Flag arch_has_sparse_bitmasks reports sparse support. Flag arch_has_per_cpu_cfg reports per processor configuration. Flag io_alloc_capable reports IO allocation capability.

Bandwidth control describes floor through min_bw and ceiling through max_bw with step through bw_gran and linear factor through delay_linear. Flag arch_needs_linear records linear need. Selector throttle_mode uses THREAD_THROTTLE_UNDEFINED for unset and THREAD_THROTTLE_MAX for chip wide and THREAD_THROTTLE_PER_THREAD for per thread. Flag mba_sc records software control. Pointer mb_map holds mapping table.

Scope RESCTRL_L2_CACHE equals two and RESCTRL_L3_CACHE equals three with RESCTRL_L3_NODE and RESCTRL_PACKAGE following. Format RESCTRL_SCHEMA_BITMAP selects bitmap and RESCTRL_SCHEMA_RANGE selects range.

Monitoring capability holds identifier count in num_rmid and configuration mask in mbm_cfg_mask with counter count in num_mbm_cntrs. Flags describe assignability through mbm_cntr_assignable and mkdir assignment through mbm_assign_on_mkdir and configurability through mbm_cntr_configurable and fixed assignment through mbm_cntr_assign_fixed.

Resource descriptor carries level identifier and capability flags for allocation and monitoring with separate control and monitoring scopes. It embeds cache, bandwidth and monitoring subrecords and maintains control and monitoring domain lists with a name pointer, a schema format selector and a code data prioritization capability flag.

Schema object links into a list and carries a short fixed name with a format string, a configuration type, a resource link and a closid count. CPU defaults hold closid and rmid values. Monitor configuration info links a resource and an L3 domain with an event identifier and a configuration value.

Helpers expose default control lookup, bandwidth event classification, iteration over bandwidth events and indices, and closid to configuration index translation with code data prioritization handling.

Default control is full mask for bitmap schemas and maximum bandwidth for range schemas with a programming error signal otherwise. Bandwidth classification covers total through local events. Configuration index is identity without prioritization and interleaves data and code slots when enabled.
Architecture hooks provide read context validation plus neutral defaults for prefetch disable bits, pseudo lock, cycle latency and L2 and L3 residency measurements.
Reading a monitoring identifier outside interrupt disabled context may sleep, so callers must not hold atomic context when interrupts are enabled.

Maximum bandwidth value is one hundred. Overflow polling interval is one thousand. Seven transaction types occupy low bits zero through six for local and remote reads, nontemporal writes, slow memory reads and dirty victims, with a seven bit mask covering them and a count of seven transactions.

Event numbering starts at one with occupancy at one, total bandwidth at two and local bandwidth at three, followed by telemetry events and a final count marker. Bandwidth event count is local minus total plus one, and state index is event minus total.
Bridge window pairs a resource in CPU address space with a translation offset. List entry wraps a resource pointer with an offset and embedded default storage, linked through a list node.
List helpers provide head and tail insertion, removal, entry release, combined destroy, iteration with safe variant, and first match lookup by resource type with absence indication.

Restart record supports blocking call restart with architecture data and a resume callback. A union carries futex state with addresses, value, flags, bitset and time, or nanosleep state with clock, type selector among none native and compat with dual remaining pointer forms and expiry, or poll state with user array, count, timeout flag and deadline.

Notification path sets a resume flag and wakes the target only on transition. Resume path clears the flag with ordering against task work arrival, then runs pending task work, releases any cached key, applies memory and block throttling, and handles restartable sequences.

Handler type receives node, data, status and registers. Hook object holds private data, an RCU protected handler pointer, an object pool and an RCU head. Node holds an RCU head, a lockfree list link, a back pointer, a return address and a frame value.
Trampoline test compares an address against the architecture trampoline symbol. Task flush is defined as a no operation in this configuration.

Trace event header packs a five bit type length with a twenty seven bit delta and a flexible payload. Type space reserves values up to twenty eight for data length with padding, time extend and timestamp markers. Flags select overwrite and testing modes. A negative one constant addresses all processors, and CPU prepare is defined as null.

Per CPU descriptor records processor number, page count excluding metadata, metadata address and a counted page array. Trace descriptor records processor count, structure length and embedded descriptors with helpers to locate first and next entries. Remote attachment holds a descriptor pointer with reader swap and reset callbacks plus private data.

Allocation helpers create local, ranged and remote buffers with per site lock keys, plus a boolean condition callback type, a swap operation reporting unsupported in this configuration, page count and descriptor size computation, descriptor iteration, and remote allocation.

Timestamp shift is twenty seven with matching mask and overflow test. Header sizes derive from page and event offsets. Base alignment is four with small data limit as alignment times twenty eight and minimum event size eight. Two build variants select native or forced eight byte alignment with matching arch alignment and data attribute.
Page layout holds a sixty four bit timestamp, a local commit index and aligned data area. Timestamp test reports whether a delta exceeds the masked range.

Rolling buffer tracks producer head and consumer tail queues with an iterator for remaining data and slot indices for next insertion and first removal. Snapshot records current queue segment, slot and folio order for iteration.
Two mark bits identify positions one and two. Advance moves the internal iterator by a byte count. Read only data test is a no operation stub in this configuration.
Root aliases are 255 for NFS and 254 for CIFS and 253 for generic under unnamed major, plus ramdisk zero for initial ram.

RTC operations vector covers ioctl, time and alarm access, proc output, alarm enable, offset handling and parameter access. Timer node combines a timer queue entry with a period, a callback receiving the device, a back pointer and an enabled flag.

RTC device embeds a generic device with owner, numeric id, operations pointer, character device, flags, interrupt data with lock queue and async handling, frequency limits, timer queue with alarm and update timers plus high resolution timer and work, write offset, feature bitmap, range limits and start handling, with optional update emulation state. Container helper derives the device from its embedded member. Busy and no character device are flag indices zero and one.
Helpers provide time subtraction, leap year test, alarm bounding by device maximum, device scoped operation locking, managed registration, and a not present code for host time sync.

Nine timestamp bounds cover year zero, nineteen hundred, GPS epoch, two thousand, and ends in twenty sixty three, twenty seventy nine, twenty ninety nine, twenty one ninety nine and ninety nine ninety nine.

Driver operations are serialized by a mutex accessed through lock and unlock helpers. Interrupt data, polling and emulation fields are protected by a spinlock, with timer queue and alarm timers manipulated under that discipline.

Return hook handler publication uses RCU with pooled nodes linked lockfree and reclaimed by RCU. Ring allocation sites use distinct static lock keys. Resource list links assume caller owned list with removal before release.

Restart block is single shot per blocking entry with resume callback selected by call type. RTC timers transition between disabled and queued with periodic reload. Ring events use data, padding and time extension records to maintain timestamp continuity across pages.
Each header is protected by a single include guard macro preventing multiple inclusion.

Type lookup may return absence and must be checked. Descriptor sizing saturates to maximum on overflow. Alarm requests beyond device maximum are truncated. Rolling producer and consumer indices require external coordination. Cross buffer swap is unsupported and reports absence of device.
